hints: Look closely at the name peroxyacetyl nitrate, PAN. What nitrogen-containing pollutant gas must M be to make a nitrate-type smog product?
Recall which solids release that brown gas on heating. Nitrates give nitrogen dioxide while carbonates give carbon dioxide.
Now check the formulae for correct charges. Only one valid nitrate formula can decompose to release that gas.
walkthrough:
**Identify gas M from PAN**

Think like a detective. PAN has nitrate in its name and is a photochemical smog pollutant.

It forms when nitrogen dioxide reacts with unburned hydrocarbons in sunlight. So M must be $\text{NO}_2$.

**Link M to thermal decomposition**

Now ask, what kind of solid gives $\text{NO}_2$ on heating?

Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating to the oxide plus nitrogen dioxide and oxygen:
$$2\text{X(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{XO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
Carbonates instead give $\text{CO}_2$, so they cannot be L.

**Check which formula is possible**

Calcium is $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and nitrate is $\text{NO}_3^-$, so one calcium needs two nitrates to balance charge: $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$.

Similarly, magnesium is $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and carbonate is $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, so only a 1:1 ratio works. This confirms the only possible source of $\text{NO}_2$.

options.A: Incorrect formula and so impossible. $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ with one $\text{NO}_3^-$ does not balance charge, calcium nitrate must be $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$. Even if you meant a nitrate, this written formula is wrong.
options.B: Correct. $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ is the valid calcium nitrate. On heating it decomposes: $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + 2\text{NO}_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$, giving M as $\text{NO}_2$ which then forms PAN.
options.C: Valid formula for magnesium carbonate, but wrong gas. It decomposes as $\text{MgCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgO} + \text{CO}_2$. $\text{CO}_2$ does not form PAN, so this cannot be L.
options.D: Incorrect on two counts. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ balances 1:1, so $\text{Mg(CO}_3)_2$ does not exist. Also, even a carbonate would give $\text{CO}_2$, not $\text{NO}_2$.
